approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is one of three Imposition Bills that together would replace five existing Acts and modernise the agricultural levies framework.
The package would let regulations re-establish current excise levies and customs charges, and also impose new levies on certain agricultural services.
The explanatory memorandum does not specify a start date for the changes or list which Acts are amended.
The Imposition Bills would enable regulations to set excise levies and customs charges on primary produce like grains, horticulture, red meat and poultry.
The package would let regulations impose levies for goods used in animal or plant treatment, such as the horse disease response levy.
The bills would allow levies on services that support primary industry production, for example bee pollination services.
The three bills would include consistent rules on definitions, exemptions, rates and other common matters.
The package would require consultation with affected industries before regulations change levy rates or introduce new levies.
The bills would allow an instrument to set rules for polls, including those for dairy and wool industries.
Farmers, producers, processors, exporters and agricultural industries that pay levies or charges under the agricultural levy system.
